title: Ask FINNY: Should financial advisors use Reddit?
summary: Most advisors build their online presence on LinkedIn and their firm website. Reddit rarely makes the list, and that may be a missed opportunity.
body_markdown:
Most advisors build their online presence in the same few places: LinkedIn, a firm website, maybe a newsletter. Reddit rarely makes the list. That may be a missed opportunity.


## Where the questions already are


Reddit is organized into communities called subreddits, and plenty of them are about money. People go there to ask how to roll over a 401(k), whether they can afford to retire early, or what to do with an inheritance. They ask in public, in their own words, and often before they have ever spoken to an advisor.


That's useful to an advisor in two ways. It's a window into what people are actually worried about, which can sharpen how you talk about your services everywhere else. And it's a place to be helpful where the conversation is already happening.


## Affinity communities live here too


The bigger opportunity may be outside the finance forums. Reddit has active communities for physicians, pilots, teachers, federal employees, tech workers, small business owners and nearly every other profession or interest you can name. If your practice serves a niche, that niche probably has a subreddit where members trade notes about pensions, equity compensation or student loans.


Showing up in those spaces consistently, answering questions and sharing what you know, is how an advisor becomes a familiar name in a community. Over time, some of the people you help may want to continue the conversation with you directly.


## A few caveats


Reddit isn't LinkedIn, and it comes with its own trade-offs.


**Most users are anonymous.** You won't always know who you're talking to, and members are quick to push back on anything that reads like a sales pitch. Hard selling tends to backfire. Plain, useful answers do much better.


**Your name is easy to target.** Posting under your real name builds credibility, but it also makes it easier for a bad actor to attach negative comments to you that are hard to trace or remove. Some advisors use a clearly professional account and stick to general education rather than personal back-and-forth.


As with any public channel, check with your compliance team before you start so you know how your firm handles review and recordkeeping for social media.


## The verdict


Reddit takes patience, and it rewards advisors who show up to help rather than to sell. For advisors willing to put in the time, it's one of the most overlooked places to build a presence online and meet people who could become prospects.


*Update -[FINNY is now on Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/FINNY_AI/)*
